newsitem.title: USA: US natgas stocks seen down 55-65 bcf in wkly AGAs.
newsitem.headline: US natgas stocks seen down 55-65 bcf in wkly AGAs.

text.p: U.S. natural gas storage levels were expected to fall by 55-65 billion cubic feet (bcf) when weekly American Gas Association (AGA) data are released later today, industry sources said this week.
The Reuter poll of industry players showed expectations for a drawdown ranged from 30 bcf to 90 bcf for the week ended March 7.

Traders at the lower end of the range said favorable spreads last week likely triggered some injections in the producing area that might result in a weekly gain for the region. But they said any build there would be more than offset by pressure to trim ample stocks in the East.
"I think we'll see that the East was dumping stocks, but we could see an injection in the producing region," said one Midwest trader.

In last report, overall stocks fell by 76 bcf, in line with expectations, and were still 130 bcf, or 15 percent, above year-ago. Eastern storage last week stood 198 bcf, or 56 percent, over last year. The four week average draw is 87 bcf.

For the same week last year, total inventories dropped by 118 bcf, meaning a draw today in the expected range would boost the overall surplus to 1996 to about 185 bcf. Eastern storage fell by 76 bcf last year, while producing stocks dropped by 35 bcf and western stocks by seven bcf.
